plans.objective: [DIM: functional_form] The solution space for linear constraints is rigid (low-dimensional), so N_c(w) will remain flat as w increases. | This hypothesis is the most testable because the ground truth (linear function is uniquely determined by 2 points) is analytically known and the prediction (flat N_c(w)) is straightforward to verify numerically. It also serves as a necessary baseline for the more complex fat family hypothesis. While it may seem trivial, establishing this baseline is essential before interpreting results for the fat case, and the experimental design (multi-seed, L-BFGS-B optimization) can rigorously rule out optimization artifacts that might otherwise be misinterpreted as rigidity.

steps.description: Implement the rigid constraint family function in `family.py` that generates linear constraints (y = x) for the width scan. This completes the required interface for the capacity_scan pipeline to test the hypothesis that the solution space for linear constraints is rigid (low-dimensional), predicting N_c(w) will remain flat as w increases. The existing pipeline will handle optimization, multi-seed evaluation, and trend analysis.

plans.objective: [DIM: optimization] The apparent flatness of N_c(w) for rigid families is an optimization artifact: small networks get trapped in spurious local minima that prevent zero-violation at widths theoretically sufficient, making the measured N_c(w) appear artificially increasing or flat when the true solution space is rigid.

steps.description: The hypothesis that N_c(w) flatness for rigid families is an optimization artifact requires testing whether small networks are trapped in spurious local minima. I will first verify if zero-violation is achievable (anchor point) at maximum width (50) for the rigid family (linear constraints y=ax+b) using scipy.optimize.minimize with L-BFGS-B and multiple random starts. If the anchor point is achievable, I will then run the width scan for both rigid and fat families to measure N_c(w) trends. This addresses the missing anchor point and N_c(w) table per the protocol. The prediction is that the rigid family will show flat N_c(w) (constant minimal width) while the fat family will show increasing N_c(w), confirming the theoretical expectation.
